questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even when you have a green light. Pedestrians may be in the intersection when it is not safe. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is driving behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up or challenge them, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than any train.
Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will be merging onto the road from the right side.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights in Florida?

options.text: To get the attention of other vehicles.
During clear, sunny days.
Between sunset and sunrise.
When you are tired.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise. Drive with extra care at night.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and continue driving safely. This prevents road rage and keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and into your eyes, making it harder to see. Use fog lights if your car has them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are not very important.
They are only used in construction zones.
They provide information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers stay in the correct lane, show safe passing zones, and warn drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop immediately and block the road.
Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: If your turn signals don't work, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: Use hand signals to show when you are turning if your turn signals don't work.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep downhill grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of work zones ahead. They are diamond-shaped with black letters and alert drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a travel lane?

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance.
Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you reach a safe place to pull off. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, stay within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: Does smoking while driving affect your ability to drive safely?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving ability.
No, it helps keep you alert.
Yes, it is a distraction.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while you are driving?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Steer straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake hard. Once you have control, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move left. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder, and signal every time.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle fits without damaging the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a railroad crossing gate. When you see flashing red lights or a lowered gate, stop completely. Wait until the lights stop and the gate is fully up before crossing.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: How can you avoid fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break. If you feel drowsy, pull over in a safe place and take a nap or find a place to sleep.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right?

options.text: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle on a divided highway. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down and move your vehicle out of the way. Stop and do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them back.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the other driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal in the direction you want to move. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive slowly and reduce your speed.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive slowly and at a reduced speed. Do not use high beams. Low beams light up the road and objects better in fog.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have enough money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that could affect safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the problem is repaired.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability in the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep and alcohol both reduce your ability to drive safely. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving as much as a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving as much as a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is ____.

options.text: 55 mph.
45 mph.
30 mph.
20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Always drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely handle these curves.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep to the right. There is a traffic island, median, or barrier ahead, and you must drive to the right of it.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only after you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. If anyone is injured, call 911. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: When a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You cannot stop your vehicle there at any time.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop for a short time to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The typical speeds people drive in that area.
The fastest or slowest legal speed allowed on that road.
The speed to drive during heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed allowed on that road.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for current conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers giving the right-of-way to others.
Drivers staying four seconds behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers speed. Always obey the speed limit and drive slower when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When turning left, who has the right-of-way over you?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic go first. You must also always give the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagon-shaped (eight sides). This shape is used only for stop signs. It tells drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When a traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light, what does this mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light before moving.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Is driving too slowly legal?

options.text: No, it is against the law.
Yes, it is safe for unsure drivers.
Yes, tired drivers should do this.
Yes, police officers recommend it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is against the law.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal. You cannot drive so slowly that you block or delay normal traffic. Drive with the flow of traffic and within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you to do?

options.text: Do not pass another vehicle.
You can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You can pass if you know the road ahead.
You can pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign (white rectangle with black text). You must follow its instructions. This sign prohibits passing. Do not pass other vehicles where this sign is posted.
